newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products -- Gulf gasoline diffs up again.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products -- Gulf gasoline diffs up again.

text.p: U.S. Gulf gasoline surged higher Monday as players continued bid prompt barrels higher, while New York Harbor and the Midcontinent held steady at firm differentials in quiet activity.
NYMEX gasoline ended sharply higher, deciding to focus on supply disruptions instead of news Iraq came a step closer to resuming oil sales.
September gasoline settled 1.67 cents higher at 66.74 cents a gallon, heating oil ended up 1.88 cents at 58.44 cents a gallon and crude closed up 47 cents at $20.75 a barrel.
U.S. GULF
Prompt conventional M1 gasoline differentials shot higher early in the day but pared part of that strength by the end, traders said.
Nearby M1 gasoline started the day between 0.75 and 1.00 cent over the September NYMEX price but changed hands as high as 2.25 cents over the screen in early afternoon action.
However, the prompt price sagged late in the day, with players putting the "get done" number near 2.00 cents over the September NYMEX.
"I think it was fairly thin. I talked to a lot of brokers who didn't trade anything today," one Gulf Coast player said.
Distillate trading was seen as very subdued, according to market watchers, with little change in differentials seen during the day.
NEW YORK HARBOR
New York Harbor gasoline differentials were steady but still firm in quiet afternoon activity. Some traders said they expect the strength to continue until the Merc delivery window closes next week.

"Differentials will remain firm until we get to the first Merc delivery window," said a Harbor trader. "It's more psychological but there are some people who are no way going to get enough for delivery."

Prompt barrels for M2 conventional unleaded gasoline held at 2.50/2.75 cents over the September screen, after rising about a quarter cent this morning. Any months were about even with the print, notionally.
A2 reformulated northern-grade unleaded also stayed at 6.75/7.00 cents, after easing slightly this morning. A 7.00-cent deal was done this morning.
The market took in some underlying strength from talk Tosco Corp will delay the restart of its 150,000 barrel per day catalytic cracker at its Bayway, N.J., refinery.
MIDCONTINENT

Midcontinent unleaded gasoline markets were also quiet after shedding some strength earlier this morning. Group Three unleaded held at 5.50/6.00 cents over September NYMEX futures. Any month barrels were pegged 2.25/2.50 cents over the print.
Chicago market unleaded gasoline was 5.50/6.00 cents over the print. Any month barrels were at 2.25/2.50 cents a gallon.
Group Three low sulphur diesel held at 2.00/2.25 cents for prompt barrels, after dipping a quarter cent this morning.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
